builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MixMoMo: Accelerating Extra--Large MoE Inference with Mixed--Precision GPU--NPU Execution on Mobile Devices
summary: MixMoMo replaces uniform-bitwidth MoE quantization and routing-score-based precision assignment with offline quantization-impact profiling plus activation-based runtime risk estimates, coupled with precision-structured GPU-NPU expert allocation and HVX-parallel dequantization. Its costs are a mobile-specific heterogeneous runtime, added profiling and precision-assignment complexity, and dependence on NPU vector units such as Qualcomm HVX. It can fail when offline sensitivity profiles do not match deployed activation distributions, when expert bitwidth diversity unbalances GPU-NPU allocation, and it provides no benefit on infrastructure without mobile NPUs.
rationale: The technique targets heterogeneous mobile GPU-NPU SoCs, hardware the reader does not operate, so its gains cannot transfer directly to a single 24 GB GPU or API-based deployment, though the quantization-sensitivity profiling idea is worth tracking.
technique: Mixed-precision MoE inference on mobile GPU-NPU SoCs

claims.statement: MixMoMo replaces uniform-bitwidth MoE quantization and routing-score-based precision assignment with offline quantization-impact profiling plus activation-based runtime risk estimates, coupled with precision-structured GPU-NPU expert allocation and HVX-parallel dequantization. Its costs are a mobile-specific heterogeneous runtime, added profiling and precision-assignment complexity, and dependence on NPU vector units such as Qualcomm HVX. It can fail when offline sensitivity profiles do not match deployed activation distributions, when expert bitwidth diversity unbalances GPU-NPU allocation, and it provides no benefit on infrastructure without mobile NPUs.
Average decoding speedups of 3.72x over uniform Q4_0 and 1.53x over the strongest mixed-precision MoE baseline, measured across three MoE models and five benchmarks on two mobile platforms.
